title: Tale's Edge
owned: Previously Lead Level Designer and Studio Director. Built the level-design pipeline from the ground up — blockout standards, validation gyms and metric reference systems — and led level design for the game's combat, stealth and parkour spaces. 100+ gym maps, 4 public playable builds, and the trailer level.
brief: Tale's Edge needed a level-design discipline from zero: standards, tools and a pipeline that let any space be tested and tuned in isolation, plus playable levels that prove a stealth/parkour/detective-quest loop reads clearly.
problem: A different approach to stealth, parkour and detective-style quest flow — deep emphasis on spatial readability and player guidance — built on a movement system and AI that were both being overhauled mid-development.
approach: I co-shaped the core loop with the Game Design Director by designing the spaces it plays out in. I then tuned traversal and AI encounters through constant iteration across public playtests. Hoofensmith Island, at the port edge of the Enchanted Forest, tested worldscale, tree-parkour, quests and stealth, and told the island's whole history through worldbuilding. Whisperwood Outpost went from a rough 2D map to concept art, a detailed 2D map and a 3D greybox, testing the Unreal Engine world-creation pipeline with the latest terrain plugins. The Small Bridge Encounter gym was the first test of the AI stealth overhaul: vision, sound, hearing and Rest/Feed 'Need Spots'.
result: A working LD pipeline, four public builds, a trailer level, and a stealth ruleset that scales to new maps.
reflection: Designing alongside systems that are still changing forces you to build for change — modular gyms and clear standards are what keep a moving target shippable.
summary: Built the level-design pipeline from the ground up and led level design for combat, stealth and parkour spaces.
